_meta.note: Hover glossary cards for the expertise dial (D1). Each term has one line per level and an optional 'act' line saying what a person usually changes. glossary.ts maps knob ids to terms and registers the text as addon.expertise.term.<id>.<field>. British spelling, no em dashes.

probe.label: Probe
probe.new: A few real training steps we run on a GPU to measure your job before predicting the rest.
probe.practitioner: A short real run (minutes) at one knob setting; every prediction is anchored to probes.
probe.expert: A short, seeded run of at least 2 optimiser steps; timings come from unprofiled steps, the profiler only supplies proportions.

flight_record.label: Flight record
flight_record.new: A small file holding what we measured and what we predicted. Share it or open it later.
flight_record.practitioner: Measurements, fitted models and intervals for one job, under 1 MB. Every view reads from it.
flight_record.expert: Versioned JSON (gzipped) with probes, knob grids (float16 point, lo, hi, abstain mask) and pinned model ids.

verify.label: Verify
verify.new: Runs your chosen plan for real, briefly, to check our prediction was right.
verify.practitioner: A real run of the chosen config; the result is added to the record and tightens later predictions.
verify.expert: Re-probe plus a fixed-seed loss check and an unchanged effective batch size; results feed adaptive conformal recalibration.

interval.label: Range
interval.new: Our best guess plus a low and high value. The true number usually lands inside.
interval.practitioner: A 90% prediction interval: on held-out jobs, about 9 in 10 true values fall inside it.
interval.expert: Conformalised quantile regression on log-ratio scores; marginal 90% coverage, not conditional on your config.

abstain.label: Not enough data
abstain.new: We would be guessing here, so we don't. Run a quick probe to get a real answer.
abstain.practitioner: The setting is outside what we measured, or the range is too wide to trust. A probe fixes it.
abstain.expert: Abstains outside the probed feature range, on kNN distance, interval width over ±50%, or analytical vs learned disagreement.

measured_predicted.label: Measured, predicted, extrapolated
measured_predicted.new: Solid means we saw it happen. Dashed means we worked it out. Grey means we're unsure.
measured_predicted.practitioner: Measured comes from a probe; predicted is inside the probed range; extrapolated is beyond it.
measured_predicted.expert: Status per estimate: measured, predicted (in range), extrapolated (beyond 2× the largest probed batch × sequence), abstain.

oom.label: Out of memory (OOM)
oom.new: The job needs more GPU memory than the GPU has, so it crashes.
oom.practitioner: Peak allocation exceeds GPU capacity; often hits at the first eval or a long batch, not step 1.
oom.expert: P(OOM) from predicted peak against capacity minus a safety margin; reported in bins because allocation grows in steps.
oom.act: Lower the batch or sequence length, or turn on gradient checkpointing.

peak_memory.label: Peak memory
peak_memory.new: The most GPU memory your job uses at any moment. If it passes the GPU's limit, it crashes.
peak_memory.practitioner: Max reserved memory over a step, including the eval spike and the CUDA or ROCm context.
peak_memory.expert: Weights + grads + optimiser state + activations + logits + allocator reserve (+0.5 to 1 GB context), calibrated on two probe peaks.

memory_terms.label: What fills the GPU
memory_terms.new: Memory goes to the model itself, its learning notes and the in-progress maths for each batch.
memory_terms.practitioner: Weights, gradients, optimiser state, activations, logits and the eval spike, stacked against capacity.
memory_terms.expert: Activations ≈ sbh(34 + 5as/h) bytes per layer (Korthikanti et al.); logits = batch × seq × vocab × bytes.

activations.label: Activations
activations.new: In-progress results kept from the forward pass so the model can learn from them. Grows with batch and length.
activations.practitioner: Saved intermediate tensors for backward; scale with batch × sequence length and usually dominate long-context jobs.
activations.expert: Per layer ≈ sbh(34 + 5as/h) bytes without recomputation; FlashAttention avoids storing the attention scores behind the 5as/h term.

optimiser_state.label: Optimiser state
optimiser_state.new: Extra numbers the optimiser keeps for each trainable weight. For Adam it can be bigger than the model.
optimiser_state.practitioner: Adam keeps two moments per trainable parameter: 8 to 12 bytes each with fp32 master weights.
optimiser_state.expert: AdamW: m and v in fp32 (8 B) plus optional fp32 master copy (4 B) per trainable param; appears at the first step.

logits_memory.label: Logits
logits_memory.new: The model's score for every possible next word. With long text and big vocabularies it takes lots of memory.
logits_memory.practitioner: batch × sequence × vocabulary × bytes; a hidden OOM cause at long sequence lengths.
logits_memory.expert: Often materialised in fp32 for the loss; chunked or fused cross-entropy avoids the full tensor.

gradient_checkpointing.label: Gradient checkpointing
gradient_checkpointing.new: Saves memory by redoing some maths instead of storing it. Slower, but fits bigger jobs.
gradient_checkpointing.practitioner: Recomputes activations in backward: a large memory saving for about one extra forward pass per step.
gradient_checkpointing.expert: Stores layer inputs only and recomputes the forward in backward; selective recomputation targets the attention block.
gradient_checkpointing.act: Turn it on when you are close to the OOM line.

lora.label: LoRA
lora.new: Teaches a model by training a small add-on instead of every weight. Much cheaper on memory.
lora.practitioner: Freezes the base model and trains low-rank adapters; gradients and optimiser state only for the adapters.
lora.expert: W + BA with rank r; trainable params ≈ r(d_in + d_out) per adapted matrix; no optimiser state for frozen weights.

qlora.label: QLoRA
qlora.new: LoRA on a squeezed copy of the model, so big models fit on smaller GPUs.
qlora.practitioner: 4-bit base weights with LoRA adapters on top; trades some speed for a large memory cut.
qlora.expert: NF4 base (≈0.5 B/param plus quantisation constants), bf16 compute, paged optimiser; dequantisation adds step time.

lora_rank.label: LoRA rank
lora_rank.new: How big the add-on is. Bigger can learn more but costs more memory.
lora_rank.practitioner: Adapter rank r; memory and compute grow linearly with r, quality gains flatten quickly.
lora_rank.expert: Trainable params scale with r; effective update scale also depends on alpha / r.

precision.label: Precision
precision.new: How many digits each number keeps. Fewer digits means faster and smaller, usually with no loss in quality.
precision.practitioner: bf16 mixed precision halves activation memory and uses tensor cores; fp32 is rarely needed.
precision.expert: bf16 avoids fp16 loss scaling; fp8 needs per-tensor scaling and hardware support (H100, MI300X).

quantisation.label: Quantisation
quantisation.new: Storing the model with fewer bits so it takes less memory and often runs faster.
quantisation.practitioner: 8-bit or 4-bit weights for serving or QLoRA; check quality on your own eval.
quantisation.expert: Weight-only (AWQ, GPTQ, NF4) vs weight and activation (fp8, int8); decode speed tracks bytes read per token.

sequence_length.label: Sequence length
sequence_length.new: The longest text, in tokens, one example can have. Longer uses more memory and time.
sequence_length.practitioner: Max tokens per example; activation and logits memory grow with it, attention cost grows faster.
sequence_length.expert: Memory roughly linear with FlashAttention, quadratic without; truncation rate tells you what you lose by capping it.

batch_size.label: Batch size
batch_size.new: How many examples the GPU works on at once. Bigger is faster per example until memory runs out.
batch_size.practitioner: Per-device micro-batch; effective batch = micro-batch × accumulation steps × GPUs.
batch_size.expert: Throughput saturates once kernels fill the GPU; changing it changes the effective batch, so check the learning rate.

eval_batch.label: Eval batch
eval_batch.new: How many examples are checked at once during evaluation. Too big can crash a run that trained fine.
eval_batch.practitioner: Eval often skips no_grad or keeps logits for metrics, so its peak can exceed training's.
eval_batch.expert: Eval peak = weights + activations without recompute + accumulated logits; the usual first-eval OOM.
eval_batch.act: Lower it, or wrap eval in no_grad.

packing.label: Sequence packing
packing.new: Joining short examples into one long row so the GPU doesn't waste time on blank padding.
packing.practitioner: Concatenates examples to fill the sequence length; removes padding waste on short, variable data.
packing.expert: Needs attention masking or position resets per example to avoid cross-contamination.

padding_waste.label: Padding waste
padding_waste.new: Share of GPU work spent on filler tokens that carry no data.
padding_waste.practitioner: Padded tokens over total tokens per batch; when it is high, packing usually pays off.
padding_waste.expert: 1 − Σ real lengths / (batch × max length), measured on probe batches.

step_time.label: Step time
step_time.new: How long one training step takes. Multiply by the number of steps for the whole run.
step_time.practitioner: Wall time per optimiser step, split into data, forward, backward, optimiser and communication.
step_time.expert: Measured on unprofiled steps; phase proportions from torch.profiler; scaled across GPUs by roofline plus a learned residual.

throughput.label: Throughput
throughput.new: How much work gets done per second, such as tokens or images.
throughput.practitioner: Tokens/sec (or samples/sec); on the map, edge speed shows it.
throughput.expert: Tokens/sec per GPU at steady state, excluding warm-up and compile steps.

mfu.label: MFU
mfu.new: How much of the GPU's top speed your job is actually using. Higher is better.
mfu.practitioner: Model FLOPs utilisation: useful maths per second over the GPU's peak. 30 to 50% is typical for well-tuned training.
mfu.expert: Achieved model FLOP/s over peak (PaLM); ≈ 6 × params × tokens/sec for dense transformers, ignoring attention.

dataloader_workers.label: Data-loader workers
dataloader_workers.new: Helpers that prepare data while the GPU trains. Too few and the GPU sits waiting.
dataloader_workers.practitioner: num_workers in the DataLoader; 0 means loading blocks the training loop.
dataloader_workers.expert: GPU idle share between kernels in the trace is the signal; also check pin_memory and prefetch.

torch_compile.label: torch.compile
torch_compile.new: A switch that makes PyTorch code run faster after a short warm-up.
torch_compile.practitioner: Fuses operations into faster kernels; first steps are slow while it compiles.
torch_compile.expert: Graph breaks and dynamic shapes cut the gain; exclude compile steps from timings.

gpu_idle.label: GPU idle share
gpu_idle.new: Time the GPU spends waiting for something else, usually data.
gpu_idle.practitioner: Share of step time with no kernel running; a large share points at data loading or the CPU.
gpu_idle.expert: From the trace's temporal breakdown (Holistic Trace Analysis): idle vs compute vs communication.

kv_cache.label: KV cache
kv_cache.new: Memory a model uses to remember the conversation so far while it writes. Grows with length and users.
kv_cache.practitioner: Stored keys and values per token; caps how many requests and how long a context fit at once.
kv_cache.expert: 2 × layers × kv_heads × head_dim × bytes per token; concurrency ≈ free memory / (bytes per token × average context).

prefill_decode.label: Prefill and decode
prefill_decode.new: Reading the prompt (fast, all at once) and then writing the answer (one token at a time).
prefill_decode.practitioner: Prefill is compute-bound, decode is memory-bandwidth-bound; they scale differently with batch.
prefill_decode.expert: Prefill time from a FLOPs roofline on prompt tokens; decode step from weights plus KV bytes read per step.

concurrency.label: Concurrency
concurrency.new: How many requests or tasks run at the same time.
concurrency.practitioner: Parallel requests in flight; limited by KV memory on your GPU or by rate limits on an API.
concurrency.expert: Wall time ≈ max(token limit, request limit, latency × tasks / concurrency).

group_size.label: Group size
group_size.new: How many answers the model writes for each prompt so they can be compared.
group_size.practitioner: GRPO samples G completions per prompt and learns from how their rewards differ.
group_size.expert: Advantages are rewards normalised within the group; larger G cuts zero-spread groups but raises rollout cost.

reward_spread.label: Reward spread
reward_spread.new: Whether a prompt's answers got different scores. If they all score the same, the model learns nothing from it.
reward_spread.practitioner: Groups where every completion scores the same have zero advantage and give no learning signal.
reward_spread.expert: P(zero spread) = p^G + (1 − p)^G for per-prompt pass rate p; DAPO's dynamic sampling filters them.
reward_spread.act: Raise group size, or drop prompts the model always gets right or wrong.

truncation.label: Truncation
truncation.new: Answers cut off because they hit the length limit. A cut-off answer often scores zero.
truncation.practitioner: Share of outputs that reach max new tokens; above about 10% hurts RL and eval results.
truncation.expert: Measured on probe rollouts; in synchronous RL the longest response also sets batch generation time.
truncation.act: Raise the completion length cap, or cap thinking separately.

rollout_share.label: Time spent generating
rollout_share.new: In RL training, how much of each step goes to the model writing answers.
rollout_share.practitioner: Rollout share of step time; often the biggest cost, which is why fast generation engines help.
rollout_share.expert: Phase timer over rollout, reference and reward, update and weight sync; set by max length in synchronous GRPO.

kl.label: KL drift
kl.new: How far the model has moved from where it started. Moving too fast can break it.
kl.practitioner: KL divergence to the reference model; rising KL without rising reward is a warning.
kl.expert: Per-token KL estimate vs the reference policy; watch its slope against reward.

entropy.label: Entropy
entropy.new: How varied the model's answers are. If it collapses, the model stops exploring.
entropy.practitioner: Per-token entropy of the policy; a fast fall signals entropy collapse in RL.
entropy.expert: DAPO's clip-higher (decoupled ε_low, ε_high) counters collapse.

grad_norm.label: Gradient norm
grad_norm.new: How big each learning update is. Sudden jumps can mean training is about to break.
grad_norm.practitioner: Total gradient size per step; a spike well above its recent average is an early warning.
grad_norm.expert: Rule fires at above 5× its moving average; compared alongside update-to-weight ratio per layer.

update_ratio.label: Update-to-weight ratio
update_ratio.new: How much each step changes the weights, compared with their size.
update_ratio.practitioner: Around 1e-3 is a common healthy value; above 1e-2 suggests the learning rate is too high.
update_ratio.expert: ‖ΔW‖ / ‖W‖ per layer per step, from probe steps.

divergence_risk.label: Divergence risk
divergence_risk.new: The chance the run's loss blows up and training stops making progress.
divergence_risk.practitioner: From early signals in the probes: gradient spikes, attention logits, update ratios.
divergence_risk.expert: Classifier on early-step features plus threshold rules; it can only say "no early warning signs", never "stable".

lr_range_test.label: Learning-rate margin
lr_range_test.new: How far your learning rate is from the point where training breaks.
lr_range_test.practitioner: A short sweep raises the learning rate until loss explodes; your margin is the gap to that point.
lr_range_test.expert: Smith's LR range test over 100 to 200 steps at your config; reported as "N× below where the probe diverged".

checkpoint_interval.label: Checkpoint interval
checkpoint_interval.new: How often the run saves its progress. Save often if the GPU can be taken away.
checkpoint_interval.practitioner: Steps between saves; trade save time against work lost on a preemption or crash.
checkpoint_interval.expert: Young/Daly: τ ≈ √(2δM), with δ the save time and M the mean time to interrupt.

preemption.label: Preemption
preemption.new: The cluster pauses or stops your job to give the GPU to someone else.
preemption.practitioner: Common on shared and cheap queues; your job needs to resume from a checkpoint.
preemption.expert: Modelled from your cluster's rule rather than assumed random; feeds the Monte Carlo completion dates.

wall_time_cap.label: Job time limit
wall_time_cap.new: The longest one job may run on your cluster before it's stopped.
wall_time_cap.practitioner: Slurm wall-time cap; long runs are split into segments that each fit under it.
wall_time_cap.expert: Segments sized from the step-time upper bound so each lands under the cap with a resume in between.

context_window.label: Context window
context_window.new: How much text a model can read at once. Agents fill it up a little more every step.
context_window.practitioner: Model's token limit; agent context grows with each turn's output and tool results.
context_window.expert: Input tokens at turn k ≈ system + Σ previous outputs and tool results; overflow step predicted per task.

prompt_caching.label: Prompt caching
prompt_caching.new: Reusing the unchanged start of a prompt so you pay less for it each time.
prompt_caching.practitioner: Cached input tokens are billed at a discount; works only if the stable prefix comes first.
prompt_caching.expert: Cost uses cache-read and cache-creation token counts from OTel GenAI spans per call.

reasoning_effort.label: Reasoning effort
reasoning_effort.new: How long the model thinks before answering. More thinking costs more and takes longer.
reasoning_effort.practitioner: Low, medium, high or extra-high; reasoning tokens are billed even though you don't see them.
reasoning_effort.expert: Muse Spark Open always reasons; effort sets the reasoning-token budget, which dominates triage cost.

rate_limit.label: Rate limit
rate_limit.new: The provider's cap on how much you can send per minute. Past it, requests wait.
rate_limit.practitioner: Requests and tokens per minute; above it, more concurrency adds no speed.
rate_limit.expert: Wall time bound by RPM and TPM; retries on 429 add latency tails.

cost_frontier.label: Cost frontier
cost_frontier.new: The options where you can't get faster without paying more. Pick one on the line.
cost_frontier.practitioner: Pareto line of time against dollars across GPUs or models; points off it are dominated.
cost_frontier.expert: Non-dominated set over (time upper bound, cost upper bound), with a deadline rule.

fan_out.label: Fan-out
fan_out.new: How many neighbours of each node a graph model looks at. More means more memory.
fan_out.practitioner: Neighbours sampled per hop; memory grows with hops × fan-out.
fan_out.expert: Sampled subgraph size grows as the product of per-hop fan-outs; CPU-side sampling can starve the GPU.

in_batch_negatives.label: In-batch negatives
in_batch_negatives.new: Retrieval models learn by telling right matches from wrong ones in the same batch. Bigger batches give more wrong ones.
in_batch_negatives.practitioner: Contrastive batch size sets the number of negatives; too small weakens training.
in_batch_negatives.expert: Cached-gradient contrastive training decouples negatives from memory.

repetition_exposure.label: Repetition exposure
repetition_exposure.new: How many times the model sees each low-quality document when data is reused over several passes.
repetition_exposure.practitioner: Same total tokens, different concentration: 4 passes over 5 GB repeats bad documents more than 1 pass over 20 GB.
repetition_exposure.expert: Per-document exposure histogram by quality bin; the data-constrained scaling prior treats tokens as equal quality, so rankings across quality abstain.

seeds_needed.label: Seeds needed
seeds_needed.new: How many repeat runs you need to be sure a difference is real and not luck.
seeds_needed.practitioner: From seed-to-seed loss noise in short probes, the runs per arm to detect a given gap.
seeds_needed.expert: Two-sample power analysis on matched-step loss variance at your chosen significance level.

gradient_accumulation.label: Gradient accumulation
gradient_accumulation.new: Adds up several small batches before each learning step, so you get the effect of a big batch without the memory.
gradient_accumulation.practitioner: Micro-batches summed per optimiser step; effective batch = micro-batch × accumulation × GPUs. Same memory, more time per step.
gradient_accumulation.expert: Grads accumulate over k micro-steps before one update; optimiser cost is amortised, activation memory stays at one micro-batch.

eval_no_grad.label: Eval without gradients
eval_no_grad.new: Tells the checks not to keep the extra notes needed for learning, which saves a lot of memory.
eval_no_grad.practitioner: Wraps evaluation in no_grad (or inference_mode) so activations are freed layer by layer instead of kept for backward.
eval_no_grad.expert: Without it, eval holds the autograd graph: activation memory as in training, with no recompute. Usually the cheapest OOM fix.
eval_no_grad.act: Turn it on; it changes no results.

gpu_type.label: GPU
gpu_type.new: Which graphics card runs the job. Bigger ones fit larger jobs and run faster, but cost more per hour.
gpu_type.practitioner: GPU model: sets memory capacity, speed and hourly price. A cheaper GPU that fits can still cost less overall.
gpu_type.expert: Cross-GPU step time keeps each kernel's measured efficiency, scaled by peak FLOPs and bandwidth; intervals widen off the probed GPU.

learning_rate.label: Learning rate
learning_rate.new: How big a step the model takes each time it learns. Too big and training breaks; too small and it barely moves.
learning_rate.practitioner: Peak step size for the optimiser; it does not change memory or time, but it decides whether the run is stable.
learning_rate.expert: Shown against the LR range test: the margin to the rate where the probe's loss diverged, together with warm-up and decay.

max_steps.label: Training steps
max_steps.new: How many learning steps the whole run takes. More steps means a longer, costlier run.
max_steps.practitioner: Total optimiser steps; time and cost scale with it, memory does not.
max_steps.expert: Total tokens = steps × effective batch × sequence length; drives the run's wall-clock, checkpoint count and segment split.

agent_model.label: Model
agent_model.new: Which AI model does the work in each task. Stronger models cost more per word but may need fewer tries.
agent_model.practitioner: The model behind the agent: sets price per token, speed and success rate, measured on your sampled tasks.
agent_model.expert: Per-task token and turn counts are bootstrapped from the sample for this model; another model's figures come from its own sample.

max_turns.label: Max turns
max_turns.new: The most back-and-forth steps an agent may take on one task before it stops.
max_turns.practitioner: Turn cap per task: limits runaway tasks and their cost, but cuts off tasks that needed more turns.
max_turns.expert: Context grows with every turn, so cost per task rises faster than linearly near the cap; the success curve is read from the sample.

n_tasks.label: Tasks
n_tasks.new: How many tasks the full run will do. We measured a small sample and scale it up.
n_tasks.practitioner: Size of the full run; cost and time scale from the 20 to 50 tasks sampled.
n_tasks.expert: Totals come from a bootstrap over the sampled tasks; the interval reflects the sample size.

tool_retry_cap.label: Tool retry cap
tool_retry_cap.new: How many times the agent may retry a tool that failed before giving up on it.
tool_retry_cap.practitioner: Retries per failing tool call; higher saves some tasks but adds turns, tokens and time.
tool_retry_cap.expert: Retry loops are the usual runaway pattern; the cap bounds the tail of tokens per task seen in the sample.

attention_kernel.label: Attention kernel
attention_kernel.new: Which piece of code does the attention maths. Faster ones save time and memory with the same results.
attention_kernel.practitioner: sdpa, FlashAttention 2 or eager; FlashAttention avoids storing the attention scores, so long sequences use far less memory.
attention_kernel.expert: Eager materialises s×s scores per head; FlashAttention tiles them in SRAM. Needs a supported GPU and dtype (fp16 or bf16).

clip_range.label: Clip range
clip_range.new: Limits how far each learning step can move the model, to keep RL training steady.
clip_range.practitioner: PPO-style ratio clipping at 1 − ε_low and 1 + ε_high; a higher upper bound lets rare good answers gain more.
clip_range.expert: DAPO's clip-higher decouples ε_high from ε_low (e.g. 0.28 vs 0.2) to counter entropy collapse.

model_width.label: Model width
model_width.new: How wide each layer of the model is. Wider models are smarter but bigger and slower.
model_width.practitioner: Hidden size d_model; parameters grow with its square, so memory and time grow fast as it rises.
model_width.expert: Params per block ≈ 12·d_model² (attention plus a 4× MLP); activation memory is linear in d_model.

attention_heads.label: Attention heads
attention_heads.new: How many separate attention patterns each layer learns at once.
attention_heads.practitioner: n_head splits d_model into heads; it barely changes parameter count but changes attention memory without FlashAttention.
attention_heads.expert: Head dim = d_model / n_head; the 5·a·s/h activation term grows with heads when scores are stored.

layers.label: Layers
layers.new: How many stacked blocks the model has. More layers, more memory and time.
layers.practitioner: n_layer: weights, activations and step time all scale roughly linearly with it.
layers.expert: Activation memory ≈ n_layer × s·b·h·(34 + 5as/h) bytes without recomputation.

dump_hidden_states.label: Saved model internals
dump_hidden_states.new: Whether the run saves the model's inner workings for later study. It can fill a lot of disk.
dump_hidden_states.practitioner: Writes hidden states (activations) per layer during evaluation; storage scales with tokens × layers × width.
dump_hidden_states.expert: Bytes ≈ tokens × layers saved × d_model × dtype size; often the real cost of interpretability sweeps.

encode_batch_size.label: Encode batch
encode_batch_size.new: How many texts are turned into vectors at once when building a search index.
encode_batch_size.practitioner: Batch size for embedding the corpus; bigger is faster until GPU memory runs out.
encode_batch_size.expert: Throughput saturates once the encoder fills the GPU; padding to the longest text in a batch wastes compute.

epochs.label: Epochs
epochs.new: How many times the model reads the whole dataset.
epochs.practitioner: Passes over the data; time and cost scale with it. Repeated data teaches less each pass.
epochs.expert: Exposure per document = epochs; Preflight's repetition view weighs it by data quality rather than treating tokens as equal.

eval_every.label: Eval interval
eval_every.new: How often the run stops to check how well it is doing.
eval_every.practitioner: Steps between evaluations; each eval costs time and can be the peak-memory moment.
eval_every.expert: Eval time × (steps / interval) adds to wall-clock; the first eval is where a planted eval OOM shows up.

fsdp_mode.label: FSDP mode
fsdp_mode.new: How the model is split across several GPUs to fit it in memory.
fsdp_mode.practitioner: full_shard splits weights, grads and optimiser state; shard_grad_op splits grads and optimiser only; hybrid shards within a node.
fsdp_mode.expert: Per-GPU state ≈ 16·P / N for full_shard (mixed precision Adam); more sharding, more all-gather traffic per step.

gnn_layers.label: GNN layers
gnn_layers.new: How many hops of neighbours each node learns from.
gnn_layers.practitioner: Message-passing layers; with neighbour sampling, the subgraph per seed grows with the product of fan-outs over the layers.
gnn_layers.expert: Sampled nodes per seed ≈ Π fan_out over layers; memory and sampler time follow that product.

gpu_memory_share.label: GPU memory share
gpu_memory_share.new: How much of the GPU the serving engine may claim. The rest is left for everything else.
gpu_memory_share.practitioner: vLLM's gpu_memory_utilization: the fraction reserved for weights plus KV cache; the KV pool is what is left after weights.
gpu_memory_share.expert: KV tokens ≈ (util × capacity − weights − activations) / (bytes per token); too high risks OOM beside other processes.

gpu_count.label: GPUs
gpu_count.new: How many graphics cards share the job.
gpu_count.practitioner: Data or model parallel across GPUs: faster per step, more cost per hour, plus communication overhead.
gpu_count.expert: Scaling efficiency falls as all-reduce or all-gather time grows relative to compute; measured on a multi-GPU probe.

grad_clip.label: Gradient clip
grad_clip.new: A cap on how big any one learning step can be, so one bad batch can't break training.
grad_clip.practitioner: Clips the global gradient norm (often 1.0); it does not change memory or time.
grad_clip.expert: Scales grads by min(1, c/‖g‖); frequent clipping in the probes hints the learning rate is high.

hidden_channels.label: Hidden width
hidden_channels.new: How much each node's internal description holds in a graph model.
hidden_channels.practitioner: Hidden feature size per layer; memory and time grow with it and with the sampled subgraph size.
hidden_channels.expert: Activation memory ≈ sampled nodes × hidden × layers × dtype size.

image_size.label: Image size
image_size.new: How big each image is when the model sees it. Bigger shows more detail but costs more.
image_size.practitioner: Input resolution; activation memory and time grow with pixels, so doubling the side roughly quadruples them.
image_size.expert: For ViTs tokens = (side / patch)², and attention cost grows with the square of tokens.

hnsw_links.label: HNSW links
hnsw_links.new: How many shortcuts each item keeps in the search index. More links, better recall and more memory.
hnsw_links.practitioner: HNSW M: graph degree per node; memory and build time grow with it, recall improves with diminishing returns.
hnsw_links.expert: Index bytes ≈ N × (d·4 + M·2·4); query time grows with M and ef_search.

ivf_lists.label: IVF lists
ivf_lists.new: How many buckets the search index sorts items into.
ivf_lists.practitioner: IVF nlist: more lists, faster queries but more training and lower recall unless you probe more lists.
ivf_lists.expert: A common rule is nlist ≈ 4·√N; recall depends on nprobe / nlist.

kl_beta.label: KL coefficient
kl_beta.new: How strongly RL training is held back from drifting away from the starting model.
kl_beta.practitioner: β on the KL penalty to the reference model; 0 removes the reference model and its memory.
kl_beta.expert: β = 0 drops the reference forward pass (time and memory); higher β slows drift and reward gains.

kv_cache_dtype.label: KV-cache precision
kv_cache_dtype.new: How many bits the serving engine uses to remember past words. Fewer bits fit more users.
kv_cache_dtype.practitioner: fp8 KV cache halves its memory versus bf16, so more requests or longer contexts fit.
kv_cache_dtype.expert: Bytes per token = 2 × layers × kv_heads × head_dim × dtype size; fp8 may cost a little accuracy.

log_every.label: Log interval
log_every.new: How often the run writes its progress.
log_every.practitioner: Steps between log lines; very frequent logging with a sync to the CPU can slow steps.
log_every.expert: .item() calls force a GPU sync; logging every step costs a few percent on small models.

lora_alpha.label: LoRA alpha
lora_alpha.new: How strongly the add-on's changes count.
lora_alpha.practitioner: Scales the adapter update by alpha / r; no effect on memory or time.
lora_alpha.expert: Effective update = (alpha / r)·BA; changing r without alpha changes the effective learning rate.

lora_dropout.label: LoRA dropout
lora_dropout.new: Randomly ignores part of the add-on while training, to avoid over-fitting.
lora_dropout.practitioner: Dropout on the adapter input; tiny memory and time cost.
lora_dropout.expert: Applied to x before A; set 0 for short runs where regularisation does not matter.

rl_loss_type.label: Loss type
rl_loss_type.new: How each answer's reward is turned into a learning signal.
rl_loss_type.practitioner: TRL's GRPO variants: grpo, bnpo, dr_grpo, dapo; they differ in how they normalise by length and group.
rl_loss_type.expert: dr_grpo drops length and std normalisation; dapo uses token-level averaging. Changes results, not memory.

model_length_cap.label: Max model length
model_length_cap.new: The longest conversation the serving engine accepts.
model_length_cap.practitioner: vLLM max_model_len: caps context per request; a lower cap lets the KV pool hold more requests.
model_length_cap.expert: Bounds per-request KV bytes; requests beyond it are rejected rather than truncated.

prompt_length_cap.label: Max prompt length
prompt_length_cap.new: The longest question the model is given in RL training. Longer ones are cut.
prompt_length_cap.practitioner: Truncates prompts; memory and generation time grow with it.
prompt_length_cap.expert: Prompt tokens add to every rollout's prefill and to the KV cache during generation.

temperature.label: Temperature
temperature.new: How adventurous the model's answers are. Higher means more varied.
temperature.practitioner: Sampling temperature; in RL it sets how different a group's answers are, and so how much there is to learn from.
temperature.expert: Low temperature raises P(zero reward spread) per group; it changes results, not memory.

tensor_parallel.label: Tensor parallel
tensor_parallel.new: Splits one copy of the model across several GPUs so a big model fits.
tensor_parallel.practitioner: TP degree: weights split across GPUs; more memory per GPU for KV cache, more communication per layer.
tensor_parallel.expert: All-reduce per layer over NVLink or PCIe; worth it only when the model does not fit on one GPU.

vllm_rollouts.label: Fast answer writing
vllm_rollouts.new: Uses a fast serving engine to write the answers during RL training.
vllm_rollouts.practitioner: Generates rollouts with vLLM instead of plain generate(); usually much faster, at the cost of reserved GPU memory.
vllm_rollouts.expert: Colocated vLLM reserves gpu_memory_utilization of the GPU; weight sync to vLLM each step adds time.

warmup_steps.label: Warm-up steps
warmup_steps.new: Starts learning gently for the first steps, then speeds up.
warmup_steps.practitioner: Steps of linear learning-rate warm-up; too few can make early training unstable.
warmup_steps.expert: Shown with the LR range test margin; no effect on memory or time.

weight_decay.label: Weight decay
weight_decay.new: Gently pulls weights towards zero so the model doesn't over-fit.
weight_decay.practitioner: Decoupled weight decay in AdamW; no effect on memory or time.
weight_decay.expert: Applied as w ← w − lr·λ·w each step; usually excluded from biases and norms.

prefix_caching.label: Prefix caching
prefix_caching.new: Lets the serving engine reuse the shared start of many requests, so it doesn't redo the same work.
prefix_caching.practitioner: vLLM automatic prefix caching: requests that share a prefix reuse its KV blocks, cutting prefill time.
prefix_caching.expert: Hit rate depends on how much prefix requests share; cached blocks stay in the KV pool and compete with live requests.
